A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VGD research and contain all 26 pages, including Appendices A–D. Pages 2–26 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance; the readable first-page differences permit a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation and prompt-quality experiments in Section 4, plus timing, human preference and other evaluations in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original empirical results in Section 4 and the appendices, including benchmark scores, ablations, generation times and human preferences.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 retain the same CLIP-guided LLM objective and beam-search procedure, including initialization, expansion, pruning and termination. No method component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate LAION-400M, MS COCO, Celeb-A and Lexica.art. Coverage of style transfer, prompt editing, distillation, multi-concept generation and transfer across text-to-image models is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Textual Inversion, LLaVA-1.5, LLaVA-1.5 with CLIP Interrogator, PH2P and PEZ. Comparator membership in the appendix evaluations is likewise unchanged.

E3.justification: The sampling, metrics, model configurations and evaluation procedures are identical. Both retain 100 sampled images per benchmark in Section 4.1 and 65 Lexica.art images for human evaluation in Appendix C.4.

E4.justification: The component and model ablations in Section 4.4 are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same cross-model generalization analyses, qualitative comparisons and failure cases.

E5.justification: Both specify five runs with different random seeds in Section 4.1 and show the same distribution summaries for prompt distillation in Figure 8. No statistical or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples are unchanged, including Table 1 benchmark scores, Table 7 generation times, Table 8 perplexities and Figure 11 human preferences. No result entries are added, removed or corrected.

T1.justification: The CLIP definitions and Bayes/noisy-channel reasoning in Sections 2–3, including Equations 1–8, are identical. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about gradient-free prompt inversion, interpretability, generalization and flexibility. The added code-access statement does not alter the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the CLIP and LLM ablations remain unchanged, as do the explanation of missed background objects in Appendix C.5 and the generalization limitations in Appendix D.1.

D1.justification: v2 adds an abstract statement that implementation code is available and supplies the DonghoonKim-1938/VGD GitHub link, absent from v1. Other implementation and reproducibility details are unchanged; the PDFs alone do not verify the repository's contents or functionality.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix B and the reference list are identical. No cited research or positioning relative to prior methods changes.

P1.justification: A short code-availability parenthetical is appended to the abstract, and the arXiv version/date markings are updated. The remaining wording and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added abstract link causes local text reflow and small positioning adjustments to the introduction and Figure 1 on page 1. Figure content, captions, tables and the layout of pages 2–26 remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The explicit implementation link in v2 modestly improves code discoverability and reproducibility documentation. The scientific content and appendices are unchanged, so the benefit is limited to this access information; the supplied PDFs do not establish the linked code's quality or reproducibility.
